P1.evidence: Nearly four minutes of unstructured small talk about European weather, South African cricket and Bulgarian tourism before the frame was set. Application referenced but not read back: 'I also saw, of course, your application, and I would just like to hear everything from you as well.' Three-part frame again. Agreement obtained ('Sounds good?' — 'Okay. Yeah, sounds good') and the open question ran.

P2.evidence: Age, weight and height were all delivered by the prospect in his own opening statement — 'I'm 46 years old... I weigh around 182 pounds... And I'm six feet tall' — and none of it was asked for, which the script scores as a miss regardless of the outcome. Occupation never asked in an hour-long call with a Silicon Valley prospect. No health-conditions question: pneumonia, shingles, high cholesterol and triglycerides were all volunteered and none of them was followed up. Injuries asked directly — 'any injuries pains that we should know about?' — which produced the Achilles history. Training frequency asked ('How many trainings are you doing at the moment of kettlebells a week?'). Diet asked well ('just take me to like a usual day of nutrition'). Sleep and energy absent again.

P3.evidence: The why was asked directly and repeatedly — 'What do you feel like stopped you from working hard enough on it up until now?' and 'why do you feel like you want to push through it being hard?' — and the ten-year future-pace ran twice. It produced the deepest available answer, 'otherwise I won't get to see my kids grow up', and the rep did not build on it at all; he moved to the airplane-oxygen-mask analogy instead. The children were asked about ('Do you have kids?') but never connected to the goal, and there was no reflect-back.

P4.evidence: 'What do you feel like stopped you from working hard enough on it up until now?' is a good P4c and got a straight answer: 'There was no motivation... we get stuck with life, work, kids.' The blocker was isolated further to structure — 'I forget the sequences and then I have to check which one to do what.' But the years of on-and-off gym memberships and the recently purchased home gym were never unpacked, and the scripted 'the information isn't the problem' line never ran, which is striking given the prospect said almost exactly that himself: 'knowing a lot, but not actually putting it into practice.'

P5.evidence: The settle question ran — 'Are you willing to settle for it getting worse?' — and got 'No, otherwise, why would I be here?' The rep followed it with an invented statistic ('I can tell you, like 75% of people are like, oh Richard, actually, I don't really want to put in the effort') rather than with 'why not?'. No two-year picture and no line in the sand. Against a prospect who had just disclosed pneumonia, shingles and a refused statin prescription, the cost of inaction was available in unusually concrete terms and was never built.

P6.evidence: Both questions ran before the offer, though the rep had to ask three times because the phrasing was long and the prospect twice said he did not understand. Belief: 'do you think Trevor is going to be able to give that structure?' — 'I think Trevor is going to be able to give that structure, that guidance, that little nudge, the correction.' Blocker sweep: 'would there be anything that would stop you from getting to the goal finally?' — 'Why should it? I can't think of a reason why I should.' A genuine yes before presenting.

P11.evidence: The sign-up link was sent live by text and receipt confirmed — 'I just sent it to you on messages, can you check if you got that' — 'yes, just came through' — which is more than most of this batch achieved. But no payment was collected: the rep accepted 'over the weekend I'll do it' from a prospect who was actively trying to leave the call. No agreement signed, no welcome or Skool walkthrough, and the rep deferred the rest with 'there's a few things that we have to run through' after signup. P11b is N/A because the University tier has no Trevor onboarding call.

objection_plays.detail: Two isolation-adjacent questions ran — 'Is that like a question of like 6k is just a lot or how does it sort of look for you?' and later 'is the thought just purely financial?' — and both got useful answers. Nothing else from the play: no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no credit cards, no available credit, no investments, and no offer to break the $6,000 into instalments at any point. The rep's entire response to price pressure was to descend the tier ladder from $6,000 to $3,000 to $1,000 across twelve minutes.

'Let me then think about between Caden and University.' One move ran — the blocker probe 'what sort of the thought is, is the thought just purely financial?' — and it was immediately followed not by a scripted move but by a commercial concession: the rep reversed a refusal he had given two minutes earlier and offered to credit the $1,000 toward an upgrade. The objection was closed with money rather than with any of the OA moves.

SCRIPT GAP — price-ladder interrogation. The prospect methodically extracted the entire tier structure with four sequential questions ('are there different tiers of cost?', 'and does this website list all the programs?', 'is there anything else apart from these two?', 'so what was the first program called?') and then bought the cheapest. There is no scripted guidance on whether, when or in what order to disclose tiers, and the rep ended up naming products, prices and staffing while visibly improvising. This is the single most commercially consequential gap surfaced in this batch.

SCRIPT GAP — clinical screening, again. Pneumonia, shingles, elevated lipids, a refused statin prescription and recurrent Achilles tendonitis were all on the table by minute 27. The playbook contains no step requiring the rep to establish clinical clearance, and the rep's improvised response went the wrong way: he endorsed the prospect's rejection of his physicians' advice.

notes: P6 was properly run and the link was sent live, which is better than most of this batch. Everything around the offer was improvised: three prices, three different accounts of the upgrade-credit policy, product names and internal staffing disclosed on the fly, and a $6,000 opportunity walked down to $1,000 in twelve minutes without a single financial-picture question being asked. Coach the pricing conversation as a defined sequence — what is disclosed, when, and on what conditions — before coaching anything else on this call.
